implement: legion-worker: the phase's PR body, proof-on-a-production-like-surface and push rules (references/pr-body.md); the architect forbids dispatching release.yaml from the branch, so the proof is T0's legion-smoke run, the differential version check and the tests
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass once the shared release-push.sh command and the checker settle
dispatch: the production check's records go on the Dispatch issue (run ids, observations), never as progress messages
test: legion-worker: the tester runs the application (the scripts against a bare origin, the checker against mutated workflows, the legion-smoke run's log), not CI again; references/pr-body.md for what it verifies and records
review: legion-worker: review threads one by one, the merge gate, the GitHub review for the head read
thermonuclear-deep-review: the credential boundary (if-chain, DEPLOY_KEY placement, cache-mode) and the checker's bypasses
thermonuclear-code-quality: the shared version command, the deploy-key helper and the checker's structure

findings.finding: D3 deleted the npm first-release seed the approved spec keeps ('for a package with no tag yet, the version npm already holds'); LEGION-247's solution doc records it as the designed answer for the next package split.
findings.answer: Kept as `release-push.sh version --first-npm <npm package>` for the three npm jobs (plan I-1). Only the dead Go first-release branches go (legion's cli-v fallback, the listener's and infra's 0.1.0 constants; every Go line has a tag); without --first-npm the command refuses when no <prefix>* tag exists.

findings.finding: The listener's `--expect` recompute fails forever under `gh run rerun --failed`, which re-reads the stale handed version; docs/kubernetes.md documents --failed as the retry idiom.
findings.answer: The refusal message names the remedy (re-run the whole run so the build job computes the version again) and docs/kubernetes.md:286-290 gets the sentence (plan I-2, T5).

findings.finding: Moving the version into release_build makes the `latest` promotion depend on the agent-secrets Go build, which today runs after latest moved.
findings.answer: release_publish runs when build and docker succeeded whatever release_build did (always() guard); the latest steps are unconditional, the tag/attest/release steps need release_build success and skip != 'true' (plan I-3, §3.4).

findings.finding: The outputs/needs/if table was unsettled; a predecessor's failed build would read as 'skipped' unless both halves are in needs; the spec's 'publish side's outputs' parenthetical conflicts with taking plugin versions from legion_build.
findings.answer: §3.3 table gives every job's needs, if, permissions and outputs; each publish job lists its predecessor's build and publish jobs and requires both in (success, skipped). legion_version comes from legion_publish; the plugin versions from legion_build, which resolves them from pi_*_publish outputs (what this run published) — the only wiring that keeps today's value on a plugin-only change (plan I-4, reported to the architect).

findings.finding: worker_image_release_note holds contents: write with steps and no decision covered it.
findings.answer: cache-mode: none; needs [legion_publish, worker_image]; if reads needs.legion_publish.outputs.tag != ''; RELEASE_TAG from legion_publish; a skipped publish yields an empty tag so the note stays skipped (§3.3).

findings.finding: 'Runs no dependency code' had no checker-holdable definition; the pattern list was asymmetric (setup-buildx-action unlisted while it may stay in the credentialed job).
findings.answer: §3.2: a deny-list of dependency-code commands in command position for run:, plus an allow-list of five actions for credentialed jobs (checkout, download-artifact, setup-node, attest-build-provenance, login-action; any other uses: fails). setup-buildx-action is dropped from the listener's publish job; if imagetools create needs it, it is restored and added to the allow-list deliberately. The header and the plan call both the checker and the build-job step tripwires, not proofs.

findings.finding: A regex over whole run: strings over-matches comments and misses `$TOOL install` or a new composite action; 'a build job' was undefined for the checker.
findings.answer: The tokenizer matches command position only (after splitting on newlines, ;, &&, ||, |, (, {, $(, backticks; comment-only lines dropped; VAR=value and shell keywords skipped); 'build job' = a job matching the patterns or the build-tool actions; tests cover `bun` in a comment passing and `go` after && failing (§3.2).

findings.finding: `docker buildx imagetools create` without setup-buildx-action is unverified and cannot be smoked on legion-smoke.
findings.answer: T0 measures `imagetools inspect --raw` without the action; the merge-triggered listener run measures `create` (latest promotion runs on that commit); a failure is a one-line restore of the pinned action (§3.4, §8, §9).

findings.finding: `agent-secrets --version` on 'each binary it built' is narrowed: only linux/amd64 executes on the runner; `go version -m` recording -ldflags was unverified.
findings.answer: Measured: Go 1.26.8 records `build -ldflags="-X …"` for a darwin/arm64 cross-build. Plan D-A: --version on linux/amd64 (prints `agent-secrets <tag>`, main.go:182) and `go version -m` on all six; recorded as a spec departure for the architect.

findings.finding: The hand-over contract per artifact set was unspecified (handed refuses any extra entry, SHA256SUMS must be written after; the listener merges two artifact sets; Bun's scoped tarball name).
findings.answer: §3.6 table: artifact names, contents and the exact handed call per publish job; legion_build no longer writes SHA256SUMS (legion_publish does); the listener downloads with merge-multiple into assets/; the npm publish jobs derive `<scope>-<name>-<version>.tgz` from their own checkout's manifest.

findings.finding: The pi plugins' manifest rewrite/restore dance had no home; three documents assert the old order.
findings.answer: The rewrite stays in the build job (tree discarded), 'Restore committed manifest' is dropped, the publish job's bump touches .version only; pack-plugin.sh, scripts/e2e/README.md and the release-bump-push solution doc are corrected (T5).

findings.finding: No documentation criterion; more docs name the moved jobs and steps than the context listed.
findings.answer: T5 lists every current document to update (envoy and infra AGENTS.md, docs/kubernetes.md, plugin READMEs, worker.Dockerfile comments, scripts/e2e files, the release-bump-push doc, root AGENTS.md Conventions) with a grep that must find nothing stale; historical docs/solutions entries are left. Reported to the architect as a scope call.

findings.finding: push-main's `git push origin main` depends on the checkout ref; the listener's publish checks out detached.
findings.answer: push-main pushes HEAD:refs/heads/main and fetches main from the git@github.com URL through the deploy-key helper; the npm publish jobs keep the event's ref; a detached-HEAD case, the missing-DEPLOY_KEY case and the key's mode/removal join release-push.test.sh (§3.1, T1).

findings.finding: The credential check's clean-runner baseline, its exit codes (`git config --get-regexp` exits 1 on no match) and the word 'proves' were unsettled.
findings.answer: §3.1 `no-credential`: captured --get-regexp, names only, exit 1 after printing every finding; T0 records the clean runner's baseline before the step is relied on; plan I-6 restates the step as a tripwire (reported to the architect).

findings.finding: Whether the npm publish jobs get `--expect` (release.yaml serialises per ref; a branch dispatch can overlap a main run).
findings.answer: Not added: the spec requires the recompute for the listener alone; today's guards (npm view skip, tag's reuse/refusal, push-tag's rejection, push-main's supersede notice) are unchanged (plan I-5, reported).

findings.finding: A rejected `cache-mode` would require changing both the workflows and the checker; the fallback shape was unnamed.
findings.answer: T0 names the fallback for the architect's approval: per-action cache inputs (setup-node package-manager-cache: false) and the checker rule 'no cache-restoring action in a credentialed job'.

findings.finding: The production-check criterion is not machine-decidable and can block indefinitely (infra may cut no release for weeks).
findings.answer: §8 gives per-workflow commands and expected output; the minimum closing bullet 10 (one npm release, one Go release); infra closes on its merge-triggered run unless the architect holds for a release (plan I-7, decision sent to the architect).

findings.finding: Contract points for the version command: locating release-bump.sh, output injection via stdout, keeping the tagged reuse, keeping latest out of it, release_build's fetch depth and needs, targets' checkout flag.
findings.answer: §3.1: sibling by its own path; exactly three validated key=value lines on stdout; tagged reuse kept including --package-dir; the latest decision stays in the workflow; release_build checks out fetch-depth 0 and release_publish needs docker so a failed image still blocks the tag; targets gains persist-credentials: false (§3.4).

specDepartures.spec: Done when, bullet 7: "The build job runs `agent-secrets --version` on each binary it built and fails unless the output is the release tag."
specDepartures.plan: release_build runs `agent-secrets --version` on the linux/amd64 binary and fails unless it prints `agent-secrets <tag>`; on every one of the six binaries (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64 agent-secrets, plus the two linux agent-secrets-helper) it runs `go version -m <binary>` and fails unless the recorded `-ldflags` build setting contains `buildversion.tag=<tag>`.
specDepartures.evidence: The release builds for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (.github/go-release-targets.json `envoy`) and darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64 (.github/agent-secrets-client-targets.json); only the linux/amd64 binary executes on an amd64 Linux runner (a Mach-O cannot; arm64 would need qemu). Measured in the workspace with Go 1.26.8: `go version -m` on a darwin/arm64 cross-build prints `build -ldflags="-X main.tag=legion-envoy-v1.2.3"`. The binary prints `agent-secrets <tag>` (packages/envoy/cmd/agent-secrets/main.go:182, version_test.go:22).

acceptance: The build job runs `agent-secrets --version` on the linux/amd64 binary it built and fails unless it prints `agent-secrets <release tag>`, and checks every binary it built with `go version -m` for the recorded `-ldflags` naming `buildversion.tag=<release tag>`, failing otherwise.
